stimuli.text: Researchers collected data from 500 adults aged 20 to 80. For each one, they recorded age and score on a timed reasoning test. The correlation between the two measures was r = −0.55.

Researchers collected data from 1,200 teenagers. For each one, they recorded the number of hours of social media use per day and score on a depression questionnaire. The correlation between the two measures was r = +0.28.

Researchers investigated whether spreading study sessions out improves long-term retention. They recruited 90 high school students and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition studied a list of 40 words in six ten-minute sessions on six different days. Participants in the other condition studied the same list in a single sixty-minute session. The researchers then recorded the number of words out of 40 that each participant recalled on a test one month later.

Researchers investigated whether mindfulness meditation lowers stress. They recruited 84 office workers and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition practiced mindfulness meditation for twenty minutes a day for eight weeks. Participants in the other condition listened to an audiobook for twenty minutes a day for eight weeks. The researchers then recorded the level of the stress hormone cortisol in a saliva sample from each participant.

Researchers investigated whether the wording of a question changes what witnesses remember. They recruited 100 adult volunteers who watched a film of a car accident and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition were asked how fast the cars were going when they smashed into each other. Participants in the other condition were asked how fast the cars were going when they contacted each other. The researchers then recorded the speed in kilometers per hour that each participant wrote down. The results are shown in the table. The difference between the two groups had a p value of 0.41.

rows.group: The group asked the question with the word 'smashed'
The group asked the question with the word 'contacted'

stimuli.text: Researchers investigated whether a phone conversation reduces what drivers notice. They recruited 64 licensed drivers and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition held a hands-free phone conversation while using a driving simulator. Participants in the other condition used the driving simulator without a phone. The researchers then recorded the number of road signs out of 30 that each participant failed to notice.

Researchers investigated whether guided hints help children learn to solve puzzles. They recruited 64 five-year-old children and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Children in one condition solved practice puzzles with hints from an adult that were gradually reduced. Children in the other condition solved the same practice puzzles alone. The researchers then recorded the number of new puzzles out of ten that each child later solved without help. The results are shown in the table. The difference between the two groups had a p value of 0.41.

Researchers investigated whether a new drug reduces anxiety. They recruited 150 adults diagnosed with generalized anxiety disorder and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition took the new drug every day for eight weeks. Participants in the other condition took a placebo pill that looked identical every day for eight weeks. The researchers then recorded each participant's score on a standard anxiety questionnaire after eight weeks.

Researchers investigated whether the color of a drink affects the ability to identify its flavor. They recruited 70 adult volunteers and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition tasted ten fruit drinks whose colors did not match their flavors. Participants in the other condition tasted the same ten drinks with matching colors. The researchers then recorded the number of flavors out of ten that each participant named correctly.

Researchers investigated whether caffeine improves attention. They recruited 80 university students and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition drank coffee containing 200 milligrams of caffeine. Participants in the other condition drank decaffeinated coffee that tasted the same. The researchers then recorded the number of targets that each participant correctly detected in a ten-minute computer task.
Researchers collected data from 250 adults. For each one, they recorded resting heart rate and self-rated anxiety. The correlation between the two measures was r = +0.38.

Researchers collected data from 400 high school students. For each one, they recorded the average number of hours slept per night and grade point average. The correlation between the two measures was r = +0.45.

Researchers collected data from 350 adults. For each one, they recorded the number of stressful life events in the past year and the number of colds in the past year. The correlation between the two measures was r = +0.33.

Researchers investigated whether praise increases hand raising in class. They recruited 50 second-grade students and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Children in one condition were praised by the teacher each time they raised a hand before speaking. Children in the other condition received no special response when they raised a hand. The researchers then recorded the number of times that each child raised a hand during one week.

Researchers investigated whether the presence of other people slows the reporting of an emergency. They recruited 80 university students and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition were filling in a form in a room with four other people when smoke began to enter the room. Participants in the other condition were filling in the form alone when smoke began to enter the room. The researchers then recorded the time in seconds before each participant left the room to report the smoke.

Read the summary of a hypothetical study, then answer parts A to F.

**Introduction.** Researchers investigated whether keeping a gratitude journal raises well-being. They hypothesized that the type of journal would affect subjective well-being.

**Participants.** The sample was 110 adult volunteers, recruited from one city. All participants gave informed consent, were told they could withdraw at any time, and were debriefed afterward. The plan was approved by an institutional review board.

**Method.** The participants were randomly assigned to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition wrote down three things they were grateful for every night for a month. Participants in the other condition wrote down three things they had done every night for a month. The researchers recorded each participant's rating of life satisfaction on a scale from 1 to 10 at the end of the month.

**Results.** The group that wrote about gratitude: mean life satisfaction (1 to 10) = 7.4. The group that wrote about daily events: mean life satisfaction (1 to 10) = 6.2. The difference was statistically significant (p = 0.01).

Use the three hypothetical sources to answer the question: **Why do people sometimes fail to help in an emergency?**

**Source A.** In an experiment, 80 students were randomly assigned to be alone or with four other people when smoke began to enter the room. Participants who were alone reported the smoke after a mean of 58 seconds; those in groups took a mean of 196 seconds (p = 0.01), and many never reported it.

**Source B.** In interviews after a staged emergency, participants who had not helped often said that they 'assumed someone else had already called for help' or that 'nobody else looked worried, so it could not be serious.'

**Source C.** Researchers observed 300 staged incidents in which a person dropped a bag of shopping in the street. Help was offered in 82 percent of incidents on quiet streets and in 41 percent of incidents on crowded streets.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes the biological perspective?

options.text: The view that disorders involve behaviors that once helped survival but are now harmful
options.why: That describes the evolutionary perspective.

options.text: The view that disorders result from genetic, brain or chemical causes
options.why: Correct. This is what the biological perspective means.

options.text: The view that disorders result from unconscious conflicts, often rooted in childhood
options.why: That describes the psychodynamic perspective.

options.text: The view that disorders result from blocked personal growth and a lack of acceptance
options.why: That describes the humanistic perspective.

questions.explanation: The biological perspective is the view that disorders result from genetic, brain or chemical causes.

questions.stem: The more hours children spend watching television, the lower their grades tend to be. Which kind of relationship is this?

options.why: Correct. A negative correlation is a relationship in which one variable rises as the other falls.
A positive correlation is a relationship in which two variables rise and fall together.
The directionality problem is the difficulty in a correlational study of knowing which variable influences the other.
A scatterplot is a graph in which each point shows one individual's values on two variables.

questions.explanation: A negative correlation is a relationship in which one variable rises as the other falls.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the ethical principle that psychologists must avoid doing harm?

options.why: Integrity is the ethical principle that psychologists must be honest and accurate.
Fidelity is the ethical principle that psychologists must be trustworthy and keep their professional promises.

options.text: Respect for people's rights and dignity
options.why: Respect for people's rights and dignity is the ethical principle that psychologists must protect privacy, confidentiality and the right of people to make their own choices.
Correct. Nonmaleficence is the ethical principle that psychologists must avoid doing harm.

questions.explanation: Nonmaleficence is the ethical principle that psychologists must avoid doing harm.

questions.stem: Which research method did the researchers use?

options.why: A case study examines one individual in depth.
Correct. The researchers measured two variables and examined their relationship without manipulating anything.
A meta-analysis combines the results of many studies.
No variable was manipulated and there was no random assignment.

questions.explanation: The researchers measured two variables and examined their relationship without manipulating anything.

questions.stem: In a noisy cafeteria, Carla follows only her friend's voice and ignores the conversations around her. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: Top-down processing is perception that is guided by experience, expectations and context.
Inattentional blindness is the failure to notice a visible object because attention is directed elsewhere.
Correct. Selective attention is the focusing of awareness on one stimulus while ignoring others.
Change blindness is the failure to notice that something in the environment has changed.

questions.explanation: Selective attention is the focusing of awareness on one stimulus while ignoring others.

questions.stem: An elderly man increasingly forgets recent events, gets lost in familiar places and can no longer manage his money. Which term describes his condition?

options.why: Correct. Dementia is a serious decline in memory and thinking that interferes with daily life, most common in old age.
Fluid intelligence is the ability to reason quickly and abstractly, which tends to decline in older adulthood.
Scaffolding is the temporary support that a more skilled person gives a learner and gradually removes.
Crystallized intelligence is the accumulated knowledge and verbal skills that tend to increase with age.

questions.explanation: Dementia is a serious decline in memory and thinking that interferes with daily life, most common in old age.

questions.stem: Gus must either clean the bathroom or wash the dishes, and he hates both. Which kind of conflict is this?

options.why: An approach-avoidance conflict is a conflict in which one option has both attractive and unattractive features.
Correct. An avoidance-avoidance conflict is a conflict in which a person must choose between two unattractive options.
An approach-approach conflict is a conflict in which a person must choose between two attractive options.
Extrinsic motivation is the desire to do something to gain a reward or avoid a punishment.

questions.explanation: An avoidance-avoidance conflict is a conflict in which a person must choose between two unattractive options.

questions.stem: Which research method did the researchers use?

options.why: No variable was manipulated and there was no random assignment.
Correct. The researchers measured two variables and examined their relationship without manipulating anything.
A case study examines one individual in depth.
A meta-analysis combines the results of many studies.

questions.explanation: The researchers measured two variables and examined their relationship without manipulating anything.

questions.stem: To teach a dolphin to jump through a hoop, a trainer first rewards swimming near the hoop, then touching it, then passing through it. Which technique is this?

options.why: Superstitious behavior is a behavior that is repeated because it happened by chance just before a reward.
A secondary reinforcer is a reinforcer, such as money or praise, that gets its power through association with other rewards.
Instinctive drift is the tendency of a trained animal to return to its natural, inborn behaviors.
Correct. Shaping is the reinforcing of closer and closer approximations of a desired behavior.

questions.explanation: Shaping is the reinforcing of closer and closer approximations of a desired behavior.

questions.stem: A researcher claims that dreams help move the day's experiences into long-term storage. Which theory of dreaming is this?

options.why: The activation-synthesis theory is the theory that dreams are the brain's attempt to make sense of random neural activity during sleep.
Memory consolidation is the strengthening of memories that takes place during sleep.
Correct. The consolidation theory is the theory that dreaming helps sort and strengthen the day's memories.
Restoration is the repair of body and brain tissue that takes place during sleep.

questions.explanation: The consolidation theory is the theory that dreaming helps sort and strengthen the day's memories.

questions.stem: A shy teenager avoids parties, so she gets little social practice, which makes her even more shy. This interaction between thoughts, behavior and environment is called which of the following?

options.why: Correct. Reciprocal determinism is the idea that a person's behavior, thoughts and environment all influence one another.
Self-efficacy is the belief in one's own ability to succeed at a particular task.
Self-concept is all the thoughts and feelings a person has in answer to the question 'Who am I?'.
Self-esteem is a person's overall feeling of self-worth.

questions.explanation: Reciprocal determinism is the idea that a person's behavior, thoughts and environment all influence one another.

questions.stem: Which group served as the control group?

options.text: The group that studied in one long session
options.why: Correct. The control group is the comparison group that does not receive the treatment being tested.
Only the comparison group is the control group.

options.text: Neither group, because the study had no comparison condition
options.why: The second condition is the comparison.

options.text: The group that studied in six short sessions
options.why: This group received the treatment being tested: it is the experimental group.

questions.explanation: The control group is the comparison group that does not receive the treatment being tested.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the reduced sensitivity that follows constant, unchanging stimulation?

options.why: Correct. Sensory adaptation is the reduced sensitivity that follows constant, unchanging stimulation.
Synesthesia is the condition in which stimulating one sense produces an experience in another sense.
Sensory interaction is the way one sense influences another, as when smell affects taste.
Transduction is the conversion of physical energy, such as light or sound, into neural impulses.

questions.explanation: Sensory adaptation is the reduced sensitivity that follows constant, unchanging stimulation.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the perception that an object keeps the same shape even when the viewing angle changes?

options.why: Size constancy is the perception that an object keeps the same size even when its image on the retina changes.
Correct. Shape constancy is the perception that an object keeps the same shape even when the viewing angle changes.
Apparent movement is the perception of motion when a series of still images or lights is shown in quick succession.
Color constancy is the perception that an object keeps the same color under different lighting.

questions.explanation: Shape constancy is the perception that an object keeps the same shape even when the viewing angle changes.

questions.stem: After a large, relaxed dinner, Ana's body directs energy toward digestion and her breathing slows. Which part of the nervous system is most active?

options.why: The somatic nervous system is the division of the peripheral nervous system that controls voluntary movement of the skeletal muscles.
The peripheral nervous system is the sensory and motor nerves that connect the brain and spinal cord to the rest of the body.
Correct. The parasympathetic nervous system is the division of the autonomic nervous system that calms the body and conserves energy.
The autonomic nervous system is the division of the peripheral nervous system that controls glands and internal organs without conscious effort.

questions.explanation: The parasympathetic nervous system is the division of the autonomic nervous system that calms the body and conserves energy.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the habit of explaining bad events as temporary, specific and caused by outside factors?

options.why: Correct. An optimistic explanatory style is the habit of explaining bad events as temporary, specific and caused by outside factors.
The actor-observer bias is the tendency to explain our own behavior by the situation but other people's behavior by their traits.
A pessimistic explanatory style is the habit of explaining bad events as lasting, affecting everything and caused by oneself.
Relative deprivation is the feeling of being worse off than the people one compares oneself with.

questions.explanation: An optimistic explanatory style is the habit of explaining bad events as temporary, specific and caused by outside factors.

questions.stem: A one-year-old says 'milk' to mean 'I want some milk'. Which stage of language development is this?

options.why: Cooing is the vowel-like sounds, such as 'ooh', that infants make from about two months.
Correct. The one-word stage is the stage from about age 1 in which a child speaks mostly in single words.
Overgeneralization is the applying of a grammar rule too widely, as in 'goed' or 'mouses'.
Babbling is the stage from about four months in which infants produce many consonant-vowel sounds, such as 'ba-ba'.

questions.explanation: The one-word stage is the stage from about age 1 in which a child speaks mostly in single words.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes rationalization?

options.text: The defense mechanism of seeing one's own unacceptable impulses in other people
options.why: That describes projection.

options.text: The defense mechanism of refusing to accept a painful reality
options.why: That describes denial.

options.text: The defense mechanism of shifting an impulse from its real target to a safer one
options.why: That describes displacement.

options.text: The defense mechanism of giving a comfortable excuse in place of the real reason for a behavior
options.why: Correct. This is what rationalization means.

questions.explanation: Rationalization is the defense mechanism of giving a comfortable excuse in place of the real reason for a behavior.

questions.stem: A psychologist shows a client a series of inkblots and asks what each might be. Which kind of test is this?

options.why: The unconscious is in psychodynamic theory, the store of thoughts, wishes and memories that a person is not aware of but that still influences behavior.
A defense mechanism is in psychodynamic theory, a method the ego uses without awareness to reduce anxiety by distorting reality.
Unconditional positive regard is the attitude of total acceptance toward another person, whatever they say or do.
Correct. A projective test is a personality test, such as an inkblot test, that asks people to interpret unclear images in order to reveal hidden feelings.

questions.explanation: A projective test is a personality test, such as an inkblot test, that asks people to interpret unclear images in order to reveal hidden feelings.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes the hypothalamus?

options.text: The wrinkled outer layer of the brain, which handles thinking, perception and voluntary movement
options.why: That describes the cerebral cortex.

options.text: The band of fibers that connects the two hemispheres of the brain
options.why: That describes the corpus callosum.

options.text: The structure that forms new explicit memories of facts and events
options.why: That describes the hippocampus.

options.text: The structure that regulates hunger, thirst, body temperature and sexual behavior and controls the pituitary gland
options.why: Correct. This is what the hypothalamus means.

questions.explanation: The hypothalamus is the structure that regulates hunger, thirst, body temperature and sexual behavior and controls the pituitary gland.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the committee that reviews research plans to make sure participants are treated ethically?

options.why: Informed consent is the agreement of participants to take part after they have been told what a study involves.
Informed assent is the agreement of a minor to take part in a study, given in addition to a parent's consent.
A confederate is a person who seems to be a participant but is secretly working for the researcher.
Correct. An institutional review board is the committee that reviews research plans to make sure participants are treated ethically.

questions.explanation: An institutional review board is the committee that reviews research plans to make sure participants are treated ethically.

questions.stem: A drug reduces pain and anxiety by acting at the brain's endorphin receptors. Which type of drug is this?

options.why: A depressant is a drug, such as alcohol, that slows neural activity and body functions.
Correct. An opioid is a drug, such as heroin, that relieves pain by acting on endorphin receptors and is highly addictive.
A stimulant is a drug, such as caffeine or cocaine, that speeds up neural activity and body functions.
A hallucinogen is a drug, such as marijuana, that distorts perception and can cause sensory experiences without sensory input.

questions.explanation: An opioid is a drug, such as heroin, that relieves pain by acting on endorphin receptors and is highly addictive.

questions.stem: For three years, Otto has felt low and tired on most days, though he still manages to work. Which disorder does this suggest?

options.why: Bipolar II disorder is the disorder in which a person alternates between depression and a milder form of mania called hypomania.
Bipolar I disorder is the disorder in which a person has full manic episodes, usually alternating with depression.
Major depressive disorder is the disorder in which a person has at least two weeks of depressed mood or loss of interest, with other symptoms such as changes in sleep and appetite.
Correct. Persistent depressive disorder is the disorder in which a person has a mildly depressed mood on most days for at least two years.

questions.explanation: Persistent depressive disorder is the disorder in which a person has a mildly depressed mood on most days for at least two years.

questions.stem: Students who are told that another group usually does badly on a test perform slightly better than usual themselves. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: A fixed mindset is the belief that intelligence is set and cannot be changed.
An achievement test is a test that measures what a person has already learned.
A growth mindset is the belief that intelligence can be developed through effort and learning.
Correct. Stereotype lift is the boost in performance that comes from awareness that another group is negatively stereotyped.

questions.explanation: Stereotype lift is the boost in performance that comes from awareness that another group is negatively stereotyped.

questions.stem: A doctor prescribes a mood stabilizer that levels out the highs and lows of a patient with bipolar disorder. Which drug is this most likely to be?

options.why: An antidepressant is a drug, such as an SSRI, that treats depression and anxiety by raising the availability of serotonin or norepinephrine.
An antianxiety drug is a drug that reduces tension by depressing central nervous system activity and can be addictive.
An antipsychotic drug is a drug that reduces hallucinations and delusions by blocking dopamine receptors.
Correct. Lithium is the mood-stabilizing drug used to treat bipolar disorder.

questions.explanation: Lithium is the mood-stabilizing drug used to treat bipolar disorder.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes an eclectic approach?

options.text: The view that disorders result from the interaction of biological, psychological and social factors
options.why: That describes the biopsychosocial model.

options.text: The view that a disorder develops when an inherited vulnerability is triggered by stressful experience
options.why: That describes the diathesis-stress model.

options.text: The presence of two or more disorders in the same person at the same time
options.why: That describes comorbidity.

options.text: The use of techniques from several types of therapy, depending on the client's problem
options.why: Correct. This is what an eclectic approach means.

questions.explanation: An eclectic approach is the use of techniques from several types of therapy, depending on the client's problem.

questions.stem: Ben is tormented by constant worry and feels miserable most of the day. Which criterion for a psychological disorder does this meet?

options.why: Deviation from the social norm is the criterion for a disorder that the behavior differs markedly from what a culture expects.
The DSM is the American Psychiatric Association's manual for classifying and diagnosing psychological disorders.
Dysfunction is the criterion for a disorder that the behavior interferes with daily life, such as work and relationships.
Correct. Distress is the criterion for a disorder that the behavior causes suffering to the person.

questions.explanation: Distress is the criterion for a disorder that the behavior causes suffering to the person.

questions.stem: Antisocial, borderline, histrionic and narcissistic personality disorders belong to which cluster?

options.why: Cluster C is the group of personality disorders marked by anxious or fearful behavior: avoidant, dependent and obsessive-compulsive.
Correct. Cluster B is the group of personality disorders marked by dramatic, emotional or erratic behavior: antisocial, borderline, histrionic and narcissistic.
A personality disorder is a lasting, rigid pattern of behavior and inner experience that differs from cultural expectations and impairs functioning.
Cluster A is the group of personality disorders marked by odd or eccentric behavior: paranoid, schizoid and schizotypal.

questions.explanation: Cluster B is the group of personality disorders marked by dramatic, emotional or erratic behavior: antisocial, borderline, histrionic and narcissistic.

questions.stem: What is the dependent variable in this study?

options.why: A hypothesis is a prediction, not a variable.

options.text: The condition to which each one was assigned
options.why: This describes the independent variable.
Correct. The dependent variable is the outcome that the researchers measured.
This was manipulated by the researchers: it is the independent variable.

questions.explanation: The dependent variable is the outcome that the researchers measured.

questions.stem: A patient describes the death of his mother in a monotone voice with no expression on his face. Which symptom is this?

options.why: Catatonia is a disturbance of movement in which a person may remain motionless for hours or move without purpose.
A hallucination is a sensory experience, such as hearing voices, that occurs without any outside stimulus.
A delusion is a false belief, often of persecution or grandeur, that a person holds despite clear evidence against it.
Correct. Flat affect is a lack of emotional expression in the face and voice.

questions.explanation: Flat affect is a lack of emotional expression in the face and voice.

questions.stem: Worried about a low grade, Deb meets her teacher, makes a study plan and joins a study group. Which kind of coping is this?

options.why: Hypertension is persistently high blood pressure, which is made more likely by chronic stress.
Correct. Problem-focused coping is the reducing of stress by changing the stressor itself or the way one deals with it.
Immune suppression is the weakening of the body's defenses against illness during long-term stress.
Emotion-focused coping is the reducing of stress by managing one's emotional reaction rather than the stressor.

questions.explanation: Problem-focused coping is the reducing of stress by changing the stressor itself or the way one deals with it.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes initiative versus guilt?

options.text: Erikson's stage in toddlerhood, in which children learn to do things for themselves
options.why: That describes autonomy versus shame and doubt.

options.text: Erikson's stage in elementary school, in which children learn to feel competent or else feel inadequate
options.why: That describes industry versus inferiority.

options.text: Erikson's stage in the preschool years, in which children learn to start tasks and carry out plans
options.why: Correct. This is what initiative versus guilt means.

options.text: Erikson's stage in infancy, in which babies learn whether their needs will be met
options.why: That describes trust versus mistrust.

questions.explanation: Initiative versus guilt is Erikson's stage in the preschool years, in which children learn to start tasks and carry out plans.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes retroactive interference?

options.text: Forgetting that happens because the information never entered long-term memory
options.why: That describes encoding failure.

options.text: The disruption of older memories by new learning
options.why: Correct. This is what retroactive interference means.

options.text: In psychodynamic theory, the pushing of anxiety-arousing memories out of awareness
options.why: That describes repression.

options.text: The pattern in which memory fades quickly at first and then levels off
options.why: That describes the forgetting curve.

questions.explanation: Retroactive interference is the disruption of older memories by new learning.

questions.stem: Which statement about the results is best supported?

options.text: The difference between the groups is statistically significant
options.why: A p value of 0.41 is far above 0.05.

options.text: The difference between the groups is not statistically significant, so it could easily be due to chance
options.why: Correct. A p value above 0.05 means a difference this size would often occur by chance alone.

options.text: The independent variable had a large effect
options.why: The averages are close and the difference is not significant.

options.text: The study shows that the two conditions always give identical results
options.why: A non-significant result does not show that there is no effect at all.

questions.explanation: A p value above 0.05 means a difference this size would often occur by chance alone.

questions.stem: Before taking part, each participant was told what the study would involve and what the risks were, and then agreed to take part. Which ethical guideline does this meet?

options.why: That is a research procedure, not an ethical guideline.
Debriefing happens after the study.
Correct. Participants must agree to take part after being told what the study involves.
Confidentiality is keeping participants' data private.

questions.explanation: Participants must agree to take part after being told what the study involves.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes boredom susceptibility?

options.text: The form of sensation seeking that involves a loss of self-restraint, as at wild parties
options.why: That describes disinhibition.

options.text: The form of sensation seeking that involves a strong dislike of repetition and routine
options.why: Correct. This is what boredom susceptibility means.

options.text: The form of sensation seeking that involves a desire for risky physical activities
options.why: That describes thrill and adventure seeking.

options.text: The form of sensation seeking that involves a desire for new experiences through travel, art and unusual lifestyles
options.why: That describes experience seeking.

questions.explanation: Boredom susceptibility is the form of sensation seeking that involves a strong dislike of repetition and routine.

questions.stem: Which statement about the results is best supported?

options.text: The difference between the groups is statistically significant
options.why: A p value of 0.41 is far above 0.05.

options.text: The difference between the groups is not statistically significant, so it could easily be due to chance
options.why: Correct. A p value above 0.05 means a difference this size would often occur by chance alone.

options.text: The independent variable had a large effect
options.why: The averages are close and the difference is not significant.

options.text: The study shows that the two conditions always give identical results
options.why: A non-significant result does not show that there is no effect at all.

questions.explanation: A p value above 0.05 means a difference this size would often occur by chance alone.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the schedule in which the behavior is reinforced after a set number of responses?

options.why: Continuous reinforcement is the schedule in which the behavior is reinforced every time it occurs.
A variable-interval schedule is the schedule in which the first response after an unpredictable amount of time is reinforced.
Correct. A fixed-ratio schedule is the schedule in which the behavior is reinforced after a set number of responses.
A fixed-interval schedule is the schedule in which the first response after a set amount of time is reinforced.

questions.explanation: A fixed-ratio schedule is the schedule in which the behavior is reinforced after a set number of responses.

questions.stem: Neither the participants nor the assistants who recorded the results knew which condition each participant was in. What is this procedure called?

options.why: Random sampling is how participants are chosen from a population.
In a single-blind procedure only the participants are unaware.
That is a therapy technique, not a research control.
Correct. Keeping both participants and researchers unaware of the conditions reduces bias from expectations.

questions.explanation: Keeping both participants and researchers unaware of the conditions reduces bias from expectations.

questions.stem: A researcher asks how much of a child's musical ability comes from genes and how much from lessons. Which theme of developmental psychology is this?

options.why: A longitudinal study is research that follows the same people and retests them over a long period.
Discontinuous development is the view that development happens in distinct stages, like a staircase.
Correct. Nature and nurture is the developmental question of how heredity and experience together shape a person.
A cross-sectional study is research that compares people of different ages at one point in time.

questions.explanation: Nature and nurture is the developmental question of how heredity and experience together shape a person.

questions.stem: The group with mismatched colors named fewer flavors correctly. The difference was statistically significant. Which conclusion is justified?

options.text: The same result would be found in every group of people or animals
options.why: The sample limits how far the result can be generalized.

options.text: The color of the drinks and flavor identification are related, but no cause can be inferred
options.why: That limit applies to correlational studies; this was an experiment.

options.text: The color of the drinks caused the difference in flavor identification
options.why: Correct. With random assignment and a manipulated variable, an experiment supports a conclusion about cause and effect.

options.text: The hypothesis has been proved, so the study need not be repeated
options.why: Findings must be replicated; one study does not prove a hypothesis.

questions.explanation: With random assignment and a manipulated variable, an experiment supports a conclusion about cause and effect.

questions.stem: Which of the following would be a confounding variable in this study?

options.text: One group differed from the other in caffeine
options.why: That is the independent variable itself.

options.text: The two groups differed in attention at the end of the study
options.why: That is the dependent variable, the result being measured.

options.text: Each one was assigned to a condition at random
options.why: Random assignment reduces confounding; it is not a confound.

options.text: The caffeine group was tested in the morning, and the decaffeinated group was tested late at night
options.why: Correct. It differs between the groups along with the independent variable, so it could explain the results instead.

questions.explanation: It differs between the groups along with the independent variable, so it could explain the results instead.

questions.stem: Lin gives up her seat on the bus to an elderly stranger who can never repay her. Which norm is guiding her?

options.why: The bystander effect is the tendency for a person to be less likely to help when other people are present.
An industrial-organizational psychologist is a psychologist who studies behavior in the workplace to improve productivity and well-being.
Altruism is unselfish concern for the welfare of others.
Correct. The social responsibility norm is the expectation that people will help those who need help, even at a cost to themselves.

questions.explanation: The social responsibility norm is the expectation that people will help those who need help, even at a cost to themselves.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the unpleasant physical and psychological symptoms that follow stopping an addictive drug?

options.why: An antagonist is a drug that decreases the action of a neurotransmitter, for example by blocking its receptors.
Correct. Withdrawal is the unpleasant physical and psychological symptoms that follow stopping an addictive drug.
Tolerance is the need for larger doses of a drug to get the same effect after repeated use.
An agonist is a drug that increases the action of a neurotransmitter, for example by mimicking it.

questions.explanation: Withdrawal is the unpleasant physical and psychological symptoms that follow stopping an addictive drug.

questions.stem: Which part of a neuron first receives a chemical message from a neighboring neuron?

options.why: The axon is the long fiber that carries the neural impulse away from the cell body toward other cells.
The axon terminals is the endings of the axon that release neurotransmitters.
Correct. A dendrite is a branching extension of a neuron that receives messages from other neurons.
The synapse is the tiny gap between the sending neuron and the receiving neuron.

questions.explanation: A dendrite is a branching extension of a neuron that receives messages from other neurons.

questions.stem: An eight-year-old answers the questions that a typical ten-year-old can answer. On Binet's test, ten is the child's what?

options.why: Correct. Mental age is the level of performance typical of a certain chronological age on an intelligence test.
General intelligence is the single underlying mental ability that Spearman believed affects performance on all mental tasks.
The intelligence quotient is originally, mental age divided by chronological age and multiplied by 100.
Multiple intelligences is the theory that people have several independent kinds of intelligence, such as musical and interpersonal.

questions.explanation: Mental age is the level of performance typical of a certain chronological age on an intelligence test.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the tendency to favor the members of one's own group?

options.why: Out-group homogeneity bias is the tendency to see the members of other groups as all alike.
Correct. In-group bias is the tendency to favor the members of one's own group.
Belief perseverance is the tendency to hold on to a belief even after the evidence for it has been discredited.
Cognitive dissonance is the discomfort a person feels when their actions and attitudes conflict, which motivates a change in one of them.

questions.explanation: In-group bias is the tendency to favor the members of one's own group.

questions.stem: Although Pat sincerely says she treats everyone equally, a reaction-time test shows she links one group with negative words more quickly. The test has revealed which of the following?

options.why: Correct. An implicit attitude is an attitude that a person holds without being aware of it.
Ethnocentrism is the tendency to judge other cultures by the standards of one's own culture.
The just-world phenomenon is the tendency to believe that people get what they deserve.
Prejudice is an unjustified negative attitude toward a group and its members.

questions.explanation: An implicit attitude is an attitude that a person holds without being aware of it.

questions.stem: After seeing a classmate praised for raising her hand, Tom starts raising his hand too. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: Correct. Vicarious conditioning is learning from seeing the consequences of another person's behavior.
Observational learning is learning by watching others and imitating them.
Latent learning is learning that takes place without reinforcement and is not shown until there is a reason to show it.
Insight learning is the sudden realization of the solution to a problem.

questions.explanation: Vicarious conditioning is learning from seeing the consequences of another person's behavior.

questions.stem: Red light and blue light differ in color. Which property of the light waves differs?

options.why: Correct. Wavelength is the distance from one wave peak to the next, which determines the hue of light.
Frequency is the number of sound waves per second, which determines pitch.
The cochlea is the coiled, fluid-filled tube in the inner ear where sound waves become neural impulses.
Amplitude is the height of a sound wave, which determines loudness.

questions.explanation: Wavelength is the distance from one wave peak to the next, which determines the hue of light.

questions.stem: Witnesses asked how fast the cars were going when they 'smashed' into each other later remember broken glass that was not there. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: Correct. The misinformation effect is the distortion of a memory by misleading information received after the event.
Constructive memory is the building of a memory at retrieval from stored pieces, expectations and later information.
Imagination inflation is the increased confidence that an event happened after repeatedly imagining it.
Source amnesia is the inability to remember where, when or how a piece of information was learned.

questions.explanation: The misinformation effect is the distortion of a memory by misleading information received after the event.

questions.stem: A patient with amnesia cannot remember practicing a puzzle, yet he solves it faster each day. Which kind of memory is still working?

options.why: Correct. Implicit memory is the memory of skills and learned associations that is retained without conscious recall.
Automatic processing is the encoding of information, such as space, time and frequency, without conscious effort.
Semantic encoding is the deep encoding of a word based on its meaning.
Effortful processing is the encoding that requires attention and conscious effort.

questions.explanation: Implicit memory is the memory of skills and learned associations that is retained without conscious recall.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes panic disorder?

options.text: The disorder in which a person has repeated, unexpected episodes of intense fear with physical symptoms such as chest pain
options.why: Correct. This is what panic disorder means.

options.text: The disorder in which a person has an intense, irrational fear of a particular object or situation
options.why: That describes a specific phobia.

options.text: The disorder in which a person feels tense and worried most of the time about many things, for at least six months
options.why: That describes generalized anxiety disorder.

options.text: The disorder in which a person fears and avoids public places from which escape might be difficult
options.why: That describes agoraphobia.

questions.explanation: Panic disorder is the disorder in which a person has repeated, unexpected episodes of intense fear with physical symptoms such as chest pain.

questions.stem: Ivo reviews his flashcards for fifteen minutes every evening for two weeks. Which kind of practice is he using?

options.why: A hierarchy is the organizing of information into broad categories divided into narrower ones.
The method of loci is the mnemonic of imagining items placed at locations along a familiar route.
A mnemonic device is a memory aid that uses vivid images or organizing tricks.
Correct. Distributed practice is study that is spread out over several sessions.

questions.explanation: Distributed practice is study that is spread out over several sessions.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes framing?

options.text: The tendency to keep investing in something because of what has already been spent on it
options.why: That describes the sunk-cost fallacy.

options.text: The way the wording of an issue affects decisions and judgments
options.why: Correct. This is what framing means.

options.text: The judging of how likely something is by how easily examples come to mind
options.why: That describes the availability heuristic.

options.text: The judging of how likely something is by how well it matches a prototype, while ignoring base rates
options.why: That describes the representativeness heuristic.

questions.explanation: Framing is the way the wording of an issue affects decisions and judgments.

questions.stem: Leo believes he is superior to everyone, expects constant admiration and has no interest in other people's feelings. Which disorder does this suggest?

options.why: Correct. Narcissistic personality disorder is the personality disorder marked by an exaggerated sense of self-importance and a need for admiration.
Avoidant personality disorder is the personality disorder marked by extreme sensitivity to rejection and avoidance of social contact.
Antisocial personality disorder is the personality disorder marked by a lack of conscience and disregard for the rights of others.
Paranoid personality disorder is the personality disorder marked by lasting distrust and suspicion of others.

questions.explanation: Narcissistic personality disorder is the personality disorder marked by an exaggerated sense of self-importance and a need for admiration.

questions.stem: Railway tracks in a drawing appear to come together at the horizon, which makes the scene look deep. Which depth cue is this?

options.why: Relative clarity is the monocular depth cue in which hazy objects are seen as farther away than sharp ones.
Retinal disparity is the binocular depth cue based on the difference between the images in the two eyes.
Correct. Linear perspective is the monocular depth cue in which parallel lines seem to meet in the distance.
Relative size is the monocular depth cue in which the object that casts the smaller image is seen as farther away.

questions.explanation: Linear perspective is the monocular depth cue in which parallel lines seem to meet in the distance.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a possible third variable that could explain the correlation?

options.why: This is the statistic, not a variable.
This is one of the two variables that were measured.

options.text: The amount of caffeine consumed each day
options.why: Correct. A third variable could influence both measures and so produce the correlation.
This is one of the two variables that were measured.

questions.explanation: A third variable could influence both measures and so produce the correlation.

questions.stem: Not wanting to upset the team's harmony, the members of a committee keep their doubts to themselves and approve a risky plan. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: Social facilitation is the improved performance on simple or well-learned tasks in the presence of others.
Deindividuation is the loss of self-awareness and self-restraint in group situations that provide arousal and anonymity.
Group polarization is the strengthening of a group's existing opinions after the members discuss them.
Correct. Groupthink is the kind of thinking in which the desire for agreement in a group overrides a realistic evaluation of alternatives.

questions.explanation: Groupthink is the kind of thinking in which the desire for agreement in a group overrides a realistic evaluation of alternatives.

questions.stem: What does the correlation show?

options.text: The first measure causes the second
options.why: A correlation does not show cause and effect.
A correlation of zero would show no relationship.

options.text: Higher values of the first measure tend to go with lower values of the second
options.why: That would be a negative correlation.

options.text: Higher values of the first measure tend to go with higher values of the second
options.why: Correct. A positive correlation means the two measures tend to move in the same direction.

questions.explanation: A positive correlation means the two measures tend to move in the same direction.

questions.stem: Which term refers to the first menstrual period?

options.why: Puberty is the period of sexual maturation, when a person becomes able to reproduce.
Correct. Menarche is a girl's first menstrual period.
Primary sex characteristics is the body structures, such as ovaries and testes, that make reproduction possible.
Menopause is the natural end of menstruation and of the ability to reproduce, usually around age 50.

questions.explanation: Menarche is a girl's first menstrual period.

questions.stem: In Jake's culture, people are praised for standing out, being independent and pursuing their own goals. Which cultural pattern is this?

options.why: Correct. Individualism is the cultural pattern that gives priority to personal goals and defines identity by personal traits.
Collectivism is the cultural pattern that gives priority to the goals of the group and defines identity by group membership.
A superordinate goal is a shared goal that can be reached only if groups cooperate, which reduces conflict between them.
A social trap is a situation in which people who each pursue their own interest end up harming everyone.

questions.explanation: Individualism is the cultural pattern that gives priority to personal goals and defines identity by personal traits.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a possible third variable that could explain the correlation?

options.why: This is the statistic, not a variable.
Correct. A third variable could influence both measures and so produce the correlation.

options.text: The number of stressful life events in the past year
options.why: This is one of the two variables that were measured.

options.text: The number of colds in the past year
options.why: This is one of the two variables that were measured.

questions.explanation: A third variable could influence both measures and so produce the correlation.

questions.stem: Two students have racing hearts before a speech; one labels the feeling as excitement and the other as fear. The difference in their emotions is due to which of the following?

options.why: An elicitor is an event or stimulus that triggers an emotion.
Correct. Cognitive appraisal is the interpretation of a situation, which shapes the emotion a person feels.
A display rule is a cultural rule about which emotions may be shown, when and to whom.
The broaden-and-build theory is the theory that positive emotions widen a person's awareness and help build lasting skills and resources.

questions.explanation: Cognitive appraisal is the interpretation of a situation, which shapes the emotion a person feels.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes recognition?

options.text: The improved recall that occurs in the same place where the information was learned
options.why: That describes context-dependent memory.

options.text: The identification of previously learned information when it is presented, as in a multiple-choice question
options.why: Correct. This is what recognition means.

options.text: The retrieval of information without any cues, as in an essay question
options.why: That describes recall.

options.text: A stimulus that helps bring a memory to mind
options.why: That describes a retrieval cue.

questions.explanation: Recognition is the identification of previously learned information when it is presented, as in a multiple-choice question.

questions.stem: The praised group raised their hands more often. The difference was statistically significant. Which conclusion is justified?

options.text: Praise from the teacher caused the difference in hand raising
options.why: Correct. With random assignment and a manipulated variable, an experiment supports a conclusion about cause and effect.

options.text: Praise from the teacher and hand raising are related, but no cause can be inferred
options.why: That limit applies to correlational studies; this was an experiment.

options.text: The hypothesis has been proved, so the study need not be repeated
options.why: Findings must be replicated; one study does not prove a hypothesis.

options.text: The same result would be found in every group of people or animals
options.why: The sample limits how far the result can be generalized.

questions.explanation: With random assignment and a manipulated variable, an experiment supports a conclusion about cause and effect.

questions.stem: Which of the following would be a confounding variable in this study?

options.text: Each one was assigned to a condition at random
options.why: Random assignment reduces confounding; it is not a confound.

options.text: The rooms used for the groups of five were much noisier
options.why: Correct. It differs between the groups along with the independent variable, so it could explain the results instead.

options.text: One group differed from the other in the number of other people present
options.why: That is the independent variable itself.

options.text: The two groups differed in the reporting of an emergency at the end of the study
options.why: That is the dependent variable, the result being measured.

questions.explanation: It differs between the groups along with the independent variable, so it could explain the results instead.

questions.stem: A five-year-old realizes that his sister will look for her doll where she left it, even though he knows it has been moved. What has he developed?

options.why: Object permanence is the understanding that things continue to exist when they are out of sight.
Correct. Theory of mind is the understanding that other people have their own thoughts, beliefs and feelings.
Animism is the belief of young children that lifeless objects have feelings and intentions.
Egocentrism is the difficulty that young children have in taking another person's point of view.

questions.explanation: Theory of mind is the understanding that other people have their own thoughts, beliefs and feelings.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the front part of the frontal lobes, which handles executive functions such as planning and self-control?

options.why: Correct. The prefrontal cortex is the front part of the frontal lobes, which handles executive functions such as planning and self-control.
The parietal lobes is the lobes at the top of the head, which process touch and spatial information.
The temporal lobes is the lobes above the ears, which process sound and help recognize language.
The frontal lobes is the lobes behind the forehead, which handle planning, judgment and voluntary movement.

questions.explanation: The prefrontal cortex is the front part of the frontal lobes, which handles executive functions such as planning and self-control.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes Broca's area?

options.text: The area in the left temporal lobe that controls language comprehension
options.why: That describes Wernicke's area.

options.text: An impairment of language caused by brain damage
options.why: That describes aphasia.

options.text: The arrangement in which each hemisphere controls the opposite side of the body
options.why: That describes contralateral control.

options.text: The area in the left frontal lobe that controls speech production
options.why: Correct. This is what Broca's area means.

questions.explanation: Broca's area is the area in the left frontal lobe that controls speech production.

questions.stem: A scan shows which brain areas receive more oxygen-rich blood while a volunteer solves puzzles. Which technique is this?

options.why: A split brain is the condition in which the two hemispheres cannot communicate because the corpus callosum has been cut.
Correct. An fMRI is a scan that shows brain activity by tracking blood flow.
A case study is an in-depth study of one individual, such as a patient with unusual brain damage.
Lesioning is the destruction of a small area of brain tissue to study its function.

questions.explanation: An fMRI is a scan that shows brain activity by tracking blood flow.

questions.stem: A child's parents and teachers meet regularly and work together. In ecological systems theory, this connection is part of which system?

options.why: The exosystem is in ecological systems theory, the settings that affect a child indirectly, such as a parent's workplace.
Correct. The mesosystem is in ecological systems theory, the relationships between the groups in a child's immediate surroundings.
The chronosystem is in ecological systems theory, the life stage and historical events that affect a child.
The macrosystem is in ecological systems theory, the cultural values, laws and customs that surround a child.

questions.explanation: The mesosystem is in ecological systems theory, the relationships between the groups in a child's immediate surroundings.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the tendency for one good quality of a person to make us assume they have other good qualities?

options.why: The peripheral route to persuasion is persuasion that works through surface cues, such as an attractive or famous speaker.
The foot-in-the-door technique is the strategy of getting agreement to a small request first so that a larger request is more likely to be accepted.
Correct. The halo effect is the tendency for one good quality of a person to make us assume they have other good qualities.
Informational social influence is the influence that comes from a person's willingness to accept others' views as evidence about reality.

questions.explanation: The halo effect is the tendency for one good quality of a person to make us assume they have other good qualities.

questions.stem: After getting food poisoning from fish, Carl feels sick at the smell of fish for years. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: One-trial conditioning is learning that happens after a single pairing of two stimuli.
Habituation is the decrease in response to a stimulus that is presented over and over.
Correct. A taste aversion is a learned dislike of a food that was followed by illness.
Counterconditioning is the replacing of an unwanted response to a stimulus with a new response, by pairing the stimulus with something pleasant.

questions.explanation: A taste aversion is a learned dislike of a food that was followed by illness.

questions.stem: Scores on a test are normally distributed with a mean of 70 and a standard deviation of 20. About what percentage of scores are between 30 and 110?

options.why: This does not match the 68–95 rule for a normal distribution.
This does not match the 68–95 rule for a normal distribution.
This does not match the 68–95 rule for a normal distribution.
Correct. About 95% of scores fall within two standard deviations of the mean.

questions.explanation: About 95% of scores fall within two standard deviations of the mean. (50 and 90 are one standard deviation from the mean; 30 and 110 are two.)

questions.title: Article analysis: a study of subjective well-being

parts.prompt: Identify the research method used in the study.

rubric.criterion: Identifies the method as an experiment.
rubric.example: The study is an experiment: the researchers manipulated a variable and randomly assigned the subjects to conditions.

parts.prompt: State the operational definition of subjective well-being.

rubric.criterion: States how the variable was measured in this study.
rubric.example: Subjective well-being was defined as each participant's rating of life satisfaction on a scale from 1 to 10 at the end of the month.

parts.prompt: Describe the meaning of the difference between the two group averages.

rubric.criterion: Accurately describes which group scored higher or lower and what that means for the variable measured.
rubric.example: The gratitude group reported higher life satisfaction. On average, the value was 7.4 for the group that wrote about gratitude and 6.2 for the group that wrote about daily events, and a p value of 0.01 means a difference this large is unlikely to be due to chance.

parts.prompt: Identify at least one ethical guideline applied by the researchers.

rubric.criterion: Identifies an ethical guideline that the summary shows was followed.
rubric.example: Informed consent: participants agreed to take part after being told about the study. (Also acceptable: debriefing; the right to withdraw; approval by an institutional review board.)

parts.prompt: Explain the extent to which the research findings may or may not be generalizable, using specific and relevant evidence from the study.

rubric.criterion: Explains a limit (or strength) of generalizability with reference to the sample.
rubric.example: The sample was 110 adult volunteers from one city, so the findings may not apply to people of other ages, cultures or backgrounds. Because the sample was not randomly selected from a wider population, it may not be representative.

parts.prompt: Explain how at least one of the research findings supports or refutes the researchers' hypothesis.

rubric.criterion: Uses a specific finding from the study as evidence.
rubric.example: The gratitude group reported higher life satisfaction. (7.4 compared with 6.2).

rubric.criterion: Explains how the finding supports the hypothesis, using a psychological concept.
rubric.example: This supports the hypothesis that the type of journal affects subjective well-being. Because subjects were randomly assigned, the difference can be attributed to the type of journal. The finding illustrates positive psychology: practicing gratitude increases subjective well-being.

questions.title: Evidence-based question: Why do people sometimes fail to help in an emergency?

parts.prompt: Propose a specific and defensible claim, based in psychological science, that responds to the question.

rubric.criterion: States a claim that answers the question and can be supported by the sources.
rubric.example: People are less likely to help when others are present, because each person feels less responsible and looks to others to decide how to act.

parts.prompt: (i) Support your claim using at least one piece of specific and relevant evidence from one of the sources. (ii) Explain how the evidence supports your claim, using a psychological perspective, theory, concept or research finding learned in AP Psychology.

rubric.criterion: Uses specific, relevant evidence from one source and names the source.
rubric.example: In Source A, participants who were alone reported smoke after 58 seconds, but those in groups of five took 196 seconds.

rubric.criterion: Explains how the evidence supports the claim.
rubric.example: This supports the claim through the bystander effect and diffusion of responsibility: when others are present, each person feels less personal responsibility to act.

rubric.criterion: Correctly applies a psychological concept in the explanation.
rubric.example: The concept must be named and applied correctly, as in the model explanation.

parts.prompt: (i) Support your claim using an additional piece of specific and relevant evidence from a different source. (ii) Explain how this evidence supports your claim, using a different psychological perspective, theory, concept or research finding.

rubric.criterion: Uses specific, relevant evidence from a different source and names the source.
rubric.example: In Source B, participants said that 'nobody else looked worried, so it could not be serious.'

rubric.criterion: Explains how the evidence supports the claim.
rubric.example: This supports the claim through informational social influence: in an unclear situation, people use the behavior of others as evidence of what is happening, so if nobody reacts, each person concludes there is no emergency.

rubric.criterion: Correctly applies a different psychological concept from the one used in part B.
rubric.example: The concept must differ from the one used in part B and be applied correctly.
